summary: Boing! Thud! Oppy’s Mars Adventure is an illustrated children’s picture book designed for lower-elementary school(grades 1-3) students that transforms NASA’s open Mars Exploration Rover data into an exciting, accessible story. Set in a lively neighborhood in the Philippines, the story follows eight-year-old Gaia as she watches Opportunity (“Oppy”) explore Mars on a tiny television at Aling Rosa’s sari-sari store. Through dynamic storytelling and real mission milestones - including icy-blue Martian sunsets, hematite “blueberries” proving that water was once accessable in Mars, the first meteorite discovered on another planet, the five-week Purgatory Ripple sand trap, and the 2018 global dust storm - young readers experience planetary science as a thrilling adventure. Inspired by Oppy’s resilience, Gaia grows up to become a chief planetary astronomer leading the first crewed mission to Mars. Complete with a factual Author’s Note detailing the real science behind the rover, this project connects the gap between complex space data and early childhood education. By setting space exploration in a familiar local community, it helps young learners everywhere to see themselves as future scientists and explorers.
details:
Our Inspiration/Why We Chose This Story :
Living in the Philippines, we see lively, sun-drenched alleys and underserved neighborhoods every day. We often see children with endless curiosity and bright eyes who rarely have access to planetariums, telescopes, or basic STEM books. Many grow up believing that space exploration belongs to people far away(privileged) - not to a child sitting on a wooden stool outside a neighborhood sari-sari store. We wanted to change that story by using a childrens book. Furthermore, as a student in an international school that is a service partner with local Phlippine schools, we occasionally work with younger children who have boundless potential and curiosity. These experiences have helped us create a child friendly and appropriate picture book for kids. Moreover, having a family member who works as an elementary school special education teacher deeply shaped our approach. Through her experiences, we learned that text-heavy science materials often leave young or neurodivergent learners/students behind. Every child deserves to feel the thrill of scientific discovery through warmth and sound.

What It Does & How It Works:
"Boing! Thud! Oppy’s Mars Adventure" is a digital and printable illustrated picture book designed for lower-elementary students (ages 6-10) and inclusive classrooms. Across eight different pages, readers follow eight-year-old Gaia in the Philippines as she watches NASA’s Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity (“Oppy”) on a sari-sari store television. The story weaves real NASA mission milestones - icy-blue Martian sunsets, hematite “blueberries” proving that Mars once held liquid water, Heat Shield Rock (the first meteorite discovered on another planet), the five-week Purgatory Ripple sand trap, and the 2018 global dust storm - into an emotional story in which Gaia growing up to become Dr. Gaia, chief planetary astronomer leading humanity’s first crewed mission to Mars. At the back of the book, an Author’s Note connects fiction and reality, introducing young readers, teachers, and adults to the real science and engineering behind Oppy’s 15-year journey.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
Our project transforms NASA’s open science data into an approachable educational tool for early-aged children and neurodiveegent children. By connecting relatable local stories, we aim to introduce STEM and remind the message to every child that no starting point is too far to reach their goals.
